title: The employee's own page: what they hold, what to confirm, their protocols
interface:
namespace Drupal\hwdesk\Controller; final class MyAssetsController extends \Drupal\Core\Controller\ControllerBase (declare(strict_types=1)). Rewrite of the existing file; keep the class and the method name page().
Three things change. (1) The page renders through the module's own template, so it looks like the rest of HW Desk instead of a bare Drupal table. (2) The employee sees their own handover protocols, which the page did not show at all. (3) The link that leads to the confirmation no longer carries a token: the mailed link is single use now, so asking for one on every page view would burn it. A logged-in employee goes to the route hwdesk.handover.confirm_own instead.
Constructor: __construct(private readonly \Drupal\hwdesk\Service\Presenter $presenter). create(ContainerInterface $container): static returns new static($container->get('hwdesk.presenter')). The HandoverService and the date formatter are no longer needed -- do not inject them, and drop their use statements.
Every row in the build comes from the Presenter, exactly like AssetController and EmployeesController do it; this class formats nothing itself, has no date format string in it and reads no entity field directly except through the typed getters named below.
page(): array -- $uid = (int) $this->currentUser()->id(). Two storages from $this->entityTypeManager(): 'hwdesk_handover' and 'hwdesk_asset'. Every query has ->accessCheck(FALSE) and is narrowed to this one employee, because the page is their own.
  $pending: handovers with condition('user', $uid), condition('status', \Drupal\hwdesk\HandoverStatus::Pending->value), sort('created', 'DESC'). For each loaded \Drupal\hwdesk\Entity\Handover take $row = $this->presenter->handover($handover) and add one key of your own: $row['confirm_url'] = \Drupal\Core\Url::fromRoute('hwdesk.handover.confirm_own', ['hwdesk_handover' => $handover->id()])->toString(). Append $row to the list.
  $assets: assets with condition('holder', $uid), condition('status', [\Drupal\hwdesk\AssetStatus::Assigned->value, \Drupal\hwdesk\AssetStatus::PendingReturn->value, \Drupal\hwdesk\AssetStatus::PendingHandover->value], 'IN'), sort('tag'). One row per asset: $this->presenter->asset($asset), nothing added.
  $handovers: the decided ones -- condition('user', $uid), condition('status', [\Drupal\hwdesk\HandoverStatus::Confirmed->value, \Drupal\hwdesk\HandoverStatus::Rejected->value], 'IN'), sort('decided', 'DESC'), range(0, 50). One row per handover: $this->presenter->handover($handover), nothing added. The protocol file's URL is already in that row under 'protocol_url'; the module's hook_file_download lets the employee download their own protocol, so no permission work belongs here.
  Return ['#theme' => 'hwdesk_my', '#account' => $this->currentUser()->getDisplayName(), '#assets' => $assets, '#pending' => $pending, '#handovers' => $handovers, '#attached' => ['library' => ['hwdesk/ui']], '#cache' => ['contexts' => ['user'], 'tags' => ['hwdesk_asset_list', 'hwdesk_handover_list']]]. The theme hook 'hwdesk_my' is declared in hwdesk.module with exactly the variables assets, pending, handovers and account; pass those four and no others.
Guard the loaded entities the way AssetController does ($x instanceof Asset / instanceof Handover) and skip anything else, so a stale reference cannot bring the page down.
No \Drupal:: static calls, no Entity::load()/loadMultiple() statics, no SQL, no '#type' => 'table'.

uses.Presenter: web/modules/hwdesk/src/Service/Presenter.php: asset(Asset $asset): array, handover(Handover $handover): array -- the row shapes the templates expect
uses.The theme hook and the download rule: web/modules/hwdesk/hwdesk.module: hwdesk_theme() declares hwdesk_my, hwdesk_file_download() guards the private files

database: The hwdesk_asset and hwdesk_handover entity storages through $this->entityTypeManager(); no direct SQL.
forbidden: Calling HandoverService::confirmUrl() or issuing a token anywhere on this page: that would spend the link from the e-mail on every page view.
Formatting dates, statuses or asset cells in the controller instead of asking the Presenter.
Showing anything that belongs to another employee.
Core '#type' => 'table' render elements: the page goes through the hwdesk_my template.
Writing the module file, the template, the Presenter or the test.
